case_title: Shahid Ali v. The State of Uttar Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.304 Part II; Arms Act s.25, s.27
confession: Confession under s.161 CrPC relied on
aggravating_circumstances: Celebratory firing during a marriage ceremony
mitigating_circumstances: No previous enmity, no intention to cause death
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide under s.304 Part II IPC
neutral_facts: The accused was present at a marriage ceremony and fired a weapon, resulting in the victim's death. The victim was shot in the neck, leading to his demise on the spot. An FIR was registered under Section 302 IPC, and a confession was obtained from the accused under Section 161 CrPC. A separate FIR was registered under Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, a post-mortem report, and an inquest report. However, all eyewitnesses turned hostile during the trial, and the trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC. The High Court upheld this conviction. The Supreme Court re-examined the case, focusing on whether the act of celebratory firing could be considered an act so dangerous as to cause death. The Court noted that there was no prior enmity and no evidence that the accused aimed at the victim. The accused was found guilty of culpable homicide under Section 304 Part II IPC, and the conviction under Section 302 IPC was set aside.
